answer: Fingerprint the hardware clock. Every machine's quartz oscillator drifts with a unique micro-signature, and when an agent emits its periodic heartbeat the protocol measures the jitter in that pulse. Honest nodes form a spreading vine of distinct timing fingerprints; a sybil fleet running a thousand masks on one backend shares a single quartz crystal, so every mask reports the same skew and collapses to one reward. Minting N identities then costs N physically distinct clocks, not one.
